Assessment Workflow

Shared reference for product owners, developers and doctors. Proposed rules remain open until agreed.

01

Purpose and Scope

Agreed requirements from the product brief.

  • Patients submit a frontpage quiz about their condition. Doctors review the assessment and decide on an appropriate care plan.
  • A care plan may include prescribed products or basic products only, depending on the doctor’s review. A prescription does not require the patient to buy the prescribed items.
  • Follow-up must support patients who buy prescribed products and patients who buy basic products without a prescription.
  • This page documents the intended workflow. It does not submit assessments, issue prescriptions, track orders or schedule reminders.

Agreed requirements from the product brief.

02

Doctor Workflow

Proposed sequence for discussion with doctors and developers.

1. Submit quiz

Owner and Action
Patient submits their answers about their condition.
Outcome / Next Step
Create an assessment linked to the patient; add Review Assessment to the doctor queue.

2. Review assessment

Owner and Action
Assigned doctor reviews answers and any available supporting information.
Outcome / Next Step
Request missing information, or continue to a care plan.

3. Request information

Owner and Action
Doctor records what is needed; patient provides a response.
Outcome / Next Step
Keep the case awaiting information until a response is available for review.

4. Record care plan

Owner and Action
Doctor records their review and chooses prescription, basic products only, or consultation / no product.
Outcome / Next Step
Save the decision and next action. Only the doctor decides whether a prescription is appropriate.

5. Track purchase

Owner and Action
Link the patient’s qualifying order to the care plan where applicable.
Outcome / Next Step
Record prescribed products purchased or basic products purchased. An unpurchased prescription remains separate.

6. Set follow-up

Owner and Action
Apply the configured timing rule; allow the doctor to set a patient-specific date.
Outcome / Next Step
Assign a follow-up owner, due date and reminder date.

7. Review progress

Owner and Action
Doctor records the patient response, progress and any concerns.
Outcome / Next Step
Continue or adjust the care plan, arrange another follow-up, or close the case with a reason.

03

Separate Statuses

Assessment, prescription, purchase and follow-up represent different events.

Assessment

Proposed Statuses
Submitted → In Review → Awaiting Information → Reviewed
Rule
Awaiting Information returns to In Review when a response arrives. Reviewed means a doctor recorded a decision, not that a purchase happened.

Care plan

Proposed Statuses
Prescription / Basic Products Only / Consultation / No Product
Rule
These are decision types, not purchase statuses. Record the reviewing doctor and decision date.

Prescription

Proposed Statuses
Draft → Issued; Cancelled where applicable
Rule
Issuing requires a doctor action. Buying a basic product must never mark a prescription as purchased or fulfilled.

Purchase

Proposed Statuses
No Qualifying Purchase / Prescribed Products Purchased / Basic Products Purchased
Rule
Derive from linked order items and the agreed qualifying order status. Mixed and partial orders need item-level matching.

Follow-up

Proposed Statuses
Unscheduled → Scheduled → Due → Completed; Cancelled where applicable
Rule
Overdue means the due date has passed and the follow-up is still open. Another follow-up is a new linked record.

Doctor Tasklist

Each task needs a patient, case link, owner, next action and due date where applicable.

New assessment

Next Action
Review Assessment
Completion Rule
Doctor starts reviewing the case.

Missing information

Next Action
Request Information
Completion Rule
Record the request; show Awaiting Patient Response rather than a completed review.

Patient responds

Next Action
Review Patient Response
Completion Rule
Doctor reviews the new information and records the next decision.

Review ready

Next Action
Complete Care Plan
Completion Rule
Save the doctor’s decision and any required prescription.

Qualifying purchase

Next Action
Set Follow-up
Completion Rule
Save an assigned follow-up with a due date, or confirm the automatically proposed schedule.

Reminder date reached

Next Action
Prepare Follow-up
Completion Rule
Make the upcoming follow-up visible to its assigned doctor. Preparing does not complete it.

Due date reached

Next Action
Review Progress
Completion Rule
Record the outcome and next action. Keep unanswered cases open with a recorded contact attempt.

Review completed

Next Action
Continue Plan / Adjust Plan / Close Case
Completion Rule
Record the decision; create the next follow-up if required.

05

Purchase and Follow-up Paths

Both purchase paths can lead to follow-up without making a prescription mandatory.

Prescribed products purchased

Linking Rule
Link patient, assessment, care plan, prescription and matching order items.
Follow-up Action
Use the prescribed-product timing rule.

Basic products purchased without prescription

Linking Rule
Link patient and order; link an assessment and care plan when available.
Follow-up Action
Use the basic-product timing rule. An assessment must not be invented to fill a missing link.

Basic products purchased after a prescription was issued

Linking Rule
Keep the prescription record separate; classify the purchased items as basic products.
Follow-up Action
Use the agreed basic-product rule; show the doctor what was actually purchased.

No purchase

Linking Rule
Keep the assessment and care plan available.
Follow-up Action
Do not start a purchase-triggered schedule. Manual follow-up and no-purchase outreach need an agreed policy.

Repeat, mixed or partial purchase

Linking Rule
Match items and retain links to previous follow-ups.
Follow-up Action
Check for an existing open follow-up before creating another; the grouping policy is pending.

Cancelled or refunded order

Linking Rule
Retain the order link and history.
Follow-up Action
Flag the existing follow-up for review. Do not silently complete or delete it.
05 · Purchase and Follow-up Paths
Path Linking Rule Follow-up Action
Prescribed products purchased Link patient, assessment, care plan, prescription and matching order items. Use the prescribed-product timing rule.
Basic products purchased without prescription Link patient and order; link an assessment and care plan when available. Use the basic-product timing rule. An assessment must not be invented to fill a missing link.
Basic products purchased after a prescription was issued Keep the prescription record separate; classify the purchased items as basic products. Use the agreed basic-product rule; show the doctor what was actually purchased.
No purchase Keep the assessment and care plan available. Do not start a purchase-triggered schedule. Manual follow-up and no-purchase outreach need an agreed policy.
Repeat, mixed or partial purchase Match items and retain links to previous follow-ups. Check for an existing open follow-up before creating another; the grouping policy is pending.
Cancelled or refunded order Retain the order link and history. Flag the existing follow-up for review. Do not silently complete or delete it.

Both purchase paths can lead to follow-up without making a prescription mandatory.

06

Follow-up Settings

Proposed configuration. No clinical timing defaults have been agreed.

Prescribed-product interval

Purpose
Days from the agreed start event to the follow-up due date.
Decision / Constraint
Doctor-approved value required; may need to vary by care plan or product.

Basic-product interval

Purpose
Separate follow-up timing for purchases without prescription.
Decision / Constraint
Doctor-approved value required.

Start event

Purpose
Choose purchase, delivery or confirmed start of use.
Decision / Constraint
Select an event that the system can reliably capture; do not substitute a missing event silently.

Reminder lead time

Purpose
Number of days before the due date that a doctor preparation task appears.
Decision / Constraint
Use a non-negative whole number that does not place the reminder before the start event.

Assigned doctor

Purpose
Owns the follow-up and its tasks.
Decision / Constraint
Agree a fallback queue when no doctor is assigned or the owner is unavailable.

Patient-specific date

Purpose
Allows the doctor to change the schedule for an individual case.
Decision / Constraint
Record who changed it, when and why; recalculate the reminder date.

Changes to defaults

Purpose
Controls whether new settings affect existing schedules.
Decision / Constraint
Proposed: apply to new follow-ups only; explicitly review changes to existing dates.
06 · Follow-up Settings
Setting Purpose Decision / Constraint
Prescribed-product interval Days from the agreed start event to the follow-up due date. Doctor-approved value required; may need to vary by care plan or product.
Basic-product interval Separate follow-up timing for purchases without prescription. Doctor-approved value required.
Start event Choose purchase, delivery or confirmed start of use. Select an event that the system can reliably capture; do not substitute a missing event silently.
Reminder lead time Number of days before the due date that a doctor preparation task appears. Use a non-negative whole number that does not place the reminder before the start event.
Assigned doctor Owns the follow-up and its tasks. Agree a fallback queue when no doctor is assigned or the owner is unavailable.
Patient-specific date Allows the doctor to change the schedule for an individual case. Record who changed it, when and why; recalculate the reminder date.
Changes to defaults Controls whether new settings affect existing schedules. Proposed: apply to new follow-ups only; explicitly review changes to existing dates.
  • Due date = agreed start date + follow-up interval.
  • Reminder date = due date − reminder lead time.
  • These reminders are internal doctor tasks. Patient email, SMS or WhatsApp reminders are not defined in this workflow.
  • Agree the clinic timezone and date boundaries before implementing due and overdue calculations.

Proposed configuration. No clinical timing defaults have been agreed.

07

Developer Reference

Proposed record boundaries and implementation requirements.

Assessment

Minimum Information
Patient reference, quiz version, submitted answers, submission date, status, assigned doctor and review history.

Care plan and prescription

Minimum Information
Assessment reference, doctor decision, notes, author and timestamps; prescribed items and issue status where applicable.

Purchase link

Minimum Information
Patient, order and item references; qualifying event timestamp; optional assessment, care plan and prescription references.

Follow-up

Minimum Information
Patient, purchase source, optional assessment / prescription, owner, timing rule snapshot, start date, due date, reminder date, status and outcome.

Task and activity history

Minimum Information
Case reference, action, owner, due date, completion event and dated actor history.
07 · Developer Reference
Record Minimum Information
Assessment Patient reference, quiz version, submitted answers, submission date, status, assigned doctor and review history.
Care plan and prescription Assessment reference, doctor decision, notes, author and timestamps; prescribed items and issue status where applicable.
Purchase link Patient, order and item references; qualifying event timestamp; optional assessment, care plan and prescription references.
Follow-up Patient, purchase source, optional assessment / prescription, owner, timing rule snapshot, start date, due date, reminder date, status and outcome.
Task and activity history Case reference, action, owner, due date, completion event and dated actor history.
  • Process repeated order events safely: the same qualifying event must not create duplicate tasks or follow-ups.
  • Keep the doctor’s decision separate from order events. Restrict prescribing and clinical review actions to authorised clinical users.
  • Preserve previous care plans and follow-up outcomes when a plan changes. Record contact attempts without marking the review completed.
  • Current dashboard patient records are demos. Production quiz, prescribing, order events, access controls and reminder scheduling still need integration.

Proposed record boundaries and implementation requirements.
